examples.knowledge_point: Solving a System of Equations to Compute an Unknown Mean or Standard Deviation
examples.problem: A data set contains the observations $x_1=18, x_2=12$ with $z$-scores $z_1=2.8$ and $z_2=1.6,$ respectively. Find the mean of the data set.
examples.worked_solution:
To compute the value of an observation $x$ which yields a given $z$-score in a data set with mean $\overline{x}$ and standard deviation $\sigma,$ we can use the following formula:

$$
x = \overline{x} + z \cdot \sigma
$$

From the first observation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}18 & =\overset{¯}{x}+2.8\cdot \sigma .\end{aligned}
$$

From the second observation, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}12 & =\overset{¯}{x}+1.6\cdot \sigma .\end{aligned}
$$

Subtracting the second equation from the first and solving for $\sigma,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}(18-12) & =(\overset{¯}{x}-\overset{¯}{x})+(2.8-1.6)\cdot \sigma  \\ 6 & =1.2\cdot \sigma  \\ \sigma  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting this value back into our first equation and solving for $\bar{x},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}18 & =\overset{¯}{x}+2.8\cdot \sigma  \\ 18 & =\overset{¯}{x}+2.8\cdot 5 \\ \overset{¯}{x} & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
